rv.q: Happily, the feats that Brynolf & Ljung engage in, while more spectacular, are also more benign.
I left pretty gobsmacked, wondering how the heck they pulled off what truly does seem like the impossible.
And it is a marvelous kind of deception — a late act with a cake is particularly jaw-dropping.
Audiences always want to be surprised and thrilled by what is incomprehensible and these two guys do fill that bill.

Peter Brynolf and Jonas Ljung's onstage presence doesn't quite match their sharp, compelling approach to magic, but Stalker is a pleasant exploration of how magic, technology, and illusion collide in the modern world.
Indeed, the premise of Stalker is that, in the post-Google world, privacy has ceased to exist.
For the 90 minutes of showtime I was sitting in a puddle of amazement.
It’s no exaggeration to say their antics caused audible gasps at the New World Stages in Manhattan’s theater district on a recent night.
This show combines street magic, illusions and physical mentalism, leaving you mystified.

cn.t: Swedish duo Brynolf & Ljung dazzle critics with their cerebral magic show, delivering prodigious feats of mentalism and illusion that amaze and befuddle audiences with sleek, entertaining psychological acrobatics.
